_comment: Carry destination for round 9's EG-B5 stage (#1743, the DHW planner extraction), from EG-B8 (#1747).
Shape and required fields: .claude/rules/finding-propagation.md. Linted by
.claude/workflows/brief_lint.mjs (the `briefs` CI job). The same carry is in the
R9-EG-B5 brief of the round-9 roster on handoff/audit-r9-fixplan; where the two

stage: round 9's EG-B5 stage: the DHW planner core moves out of HeatPumpOptimizer, and _co_optimize's replan becomes a planner call

carries.from: the pull request that lands round 9's EG-B8 (roster group R9-EG-B8: fixes #1747) -- the co-optimisation replan given the DHW mode block, and DhwProfileLearner.normalize_profile made a projection
carries.control: Established by measurement with its null control. On the tests/golden.py wood_coil scenario, DHW-blocked with its external-heat forecast and prices shifted by -2.0 (68 of 96 steps negative), the replan without the block shipped 9.22 kWh of DHW heat and reported a 0.629 K tank-floor breach; given the block it ships none and reports 20.81 K. The control is the same scenario at a shift of 0.0, where the replan is not adopted and both arms ship none.
carries.remeasure: Do not trust these figures: they are measured at EG-B8's head. Re-run tests/features.py at your merge base and read the check "a DHW-blocked plan ships no hot water when mostly negative prices tempt the co-optimisation replan (#1747)" and its companion "and every DHW build that solve made was told the mode is blocked".
carries.brief: When the replan in `_co_optimize` becomes a planner call, it keeps the block the first build receives (`blocked=h.dhw_blocked`): after EG-B8 the only keyword the two `_build_dhw_requirements` calls may differ in is `space_demand`, the space profile the replan exists to price. The class is a second call site omitting a defaulted keyword the first passes; EG-B8's pull-request body carries the AST enumerator it ran over optimizer.py (10 seams at its head, each dispositioned). Run it on the new planner module and on optimizer.py after the move, and disposition every seam it returns.

carries.from: the round-9 root-cause seat for #1747 (R9-RCA-1747), on branch handoff/rca-1747
carries.control: Established by measurement with its null control, with tools/audit/round9/rca/1747/rca_census_reach.py at EG-B8's code head 1b43198e. When the replan rebuilds through a callable the tests/features.py spy does not patch and drops the block, 9.22 kWh of DHW ships through the blocked mode (breach 0.629 K), and the check 'and every DHW build that solve made was told the mode is blocked' still passes, because the spy saw only the first build ([True]). The as-is arm (builds [True, True]) is the null control. The first #1747 check caught the perturbed arm only because its -2.0 price shift makes the replan win; at shifts 0.0 and -1.0 the replan is built and not adopted (b8_replan_blocked.py), so that check cannot see a block dropped there.
carries.remeasure: Do not trust these figures: they are measured at 1b43198e. Re-run rca_census_reach.py at your merge base, and again at your head once the replan is a planner call.
carries.brief: When `_co_optimize`'s replan becomes a planner call, the tests/features.py spy that pins #1747 patches `HeatPumpOptimizer._build_dhw_requirements` and will stop seeing the replan if the planner builds through another callable. It then passes with one build seen while the replan is unwatched. Point the spy at the callable the planner uses for both builds, and keep or add a reach clause (the replan's build is among the builds it saw) so that the check refuses rather than passes if it loses the replan. R9-F1.11 is carried the same reach clause for the P2 barrier (carry-1644.json). If F1.11 has landed it, keep it green; if it has not, add it here.
